conviction_note: Nothing company-level and unpriced was found: the Q3 guide (NII +2-2.5%, fees +1-3%, expenses -1-2%, NCO 30-35bp) was reaffirmed unchanged in the 2026-09-15 Barclays deck and the Fed hike it assumed arrived on 2026-09-16; the lean is a mild negative built from proxies (PNC fell short of its own NII guide on funding costs, big banks sold beats this week, FITB itself fell 2.29% on a beat-and-raise in July) against a stock already 15% off its high with a balanced skew, so p_up 43 on a 3.0% absolute move gives -0.42 while the findings sum to -1.0; the gap is that the findings are proxies and the reaction function is damped (median 1.31% over seven prints).
bar: Adjusted EPS $1.09 consensus (two agreeing sources: https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/FITB whisper $1.12, revenue $3.34B; https://www.alphaquery.com/stock/FITB/earnings-history $1.09) against the company's own Q3 guide of NII +2-2.5% from $2.22B, noninterest income +1-3% from $1.04B, adjusted expense -1-2% from $1.86B, NCO 30-35bp, tax 22.5%, loans +1%, reaffirmed 'unchanged from July 17' on slide 16 of the Barclays deck filed 2026-09-14 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/35527/000003552726000219/a2026barclaysconference-.htm). The guide implies revenue of roughly $3.33B, so the $3.34B consensus sits on the guide. Benzinga/TickerLeague show $0.85-0.88, which is GAAP including merger charges, not the adjusted bar the name trades on.
positioning_check: Short interest 36.26M shares at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, about 4.0% of shares outstanding, 5.05 days to cover, up from 32.2M on 09-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/fitb/shortinterest, fetched 2026-10-16; MarketBeat showed N/A on 2026-10-16 so no second source). Not crowded. Sealed skew -0.35 vol points (balanced, calls fractionally dearer), put/call open interest 0.42, option-implied event move 5.79% against a 1.31% median and 2.29% max realised over seven prints. Stock -15.25% from its 52-week high and -4.9% over 20 sessions; PNC was -12.6% since its last print as of 2026-10-06, so the drawdown is sector-wide.

findings.finding: PNC, reporting 2026-10-15, delivered Q3 NII of $4,206M, +$99M or +2.4% q/q against its own guide of +3-3.5% from a $4,107M base, with NIM down 2bp to 2.94% 'partially offset by increased funding costs'; Fifth Third's unchanged Q3 guide is NII +2-2.5% from $2.22B (i.e. $2.264-2.276B) and the July call said deposit costs would be 'stable to maybe slightly up', so a peer that just missed its own NII guide on funding costs points to the low end for FITB. Truist (2026-10-16) landed NII +1.1% inside its +1-1.5% guide and JPMorgan raised its 2026 NII outlook, so the broader peer read is mixed and this is sized as a proxy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-17): NII $2.22B, NIM +6bp, FY NII guide raised, adjusted EPS $1.02 vs $0.98 consensus, stock -2.29%; the name did not pay for an NII beat last time, so a small NII shortfall is also likely to be damped.
findings.why_not_priced: PNC reported after Fifth Third last spoke (09-15); FITB's 5-day run-up is only -0.64% through the big-bank prints and consensus revenue ($3.34B) still sits on the guide's midpoint, so the funding-cost shortfall at a peer has not moved FITB's bar. If it had, the whisper would be at or below consensus rather than $0.03 above it.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a company number. Truist Q3 ex-99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000092230/000009223026000108/ex991-3q26.htm, 2026-10-16) shows NII +1.1% in line with guide and NIM +2bp, which cuts the other way; PNC's own Q3 guide of +3-3.5% is in its Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000713676/000162828026053170/pnc-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: The reaction function this week has been to sell beats: Citigroup had its worst day since April 2025 and Wells Fargo fell about 3% on 2026-10-13 despite EPS beats, on forward guidance and a NIM that fell to 2.43%; Fifth Third's own last print (2026-07-17) was an adjusted beat with a raised FY NII guide and the stock closed -2.29%, so even a print that clears the $1.09 bar and the $1.12 whisper has a damped or negative expected reaction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: seven prints, median |move| 1.31%, four up and three down, the two largest moves both negative (-2.29% in July 2026 on a beat-and-raise, -1.02% in July 2025); beats have not been bought.
findings.why_not_priced: A reaction pattern is not in the price by construction; the sealed skew is balanced (-0.35) and put/call OI is 0.42, so the option market is not paying for downside into this print despite the week's pattern. If it were priced the skew would be positive.
findings.independence: Fifth Third's own Q2 reaction: https://www.chartmill.com/news/external/81825/fifth-third-q2-earnings-beat-on-strong-nii-fee-income-stock-down (2026-07-17) and the baseline's -2.29%. CNBC live blog for the big-bank day: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/13/bank-earnings-live-updates.html.

findings.finding: The Barclays deck filed 2026-09-14 says Q3 expectations are 'unchanged from July 17, 2026 earnings call' (NII +2-2.5% assuming a 4.00% Fed funds rate at 9/30, fees +1-3%, expense -1-2%, NCO 30-35bp, tax 22.5%) and the FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, exactly the hike the guide assumed, so there is no rate or guidance surprise in the quarter; meanwhile the whisper ($1.12) sits $0.03 above the $1.09 consensus, so the effective bar is slightly above the wire and a print that merely meets the guide reads as in-line to light.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: January 2026 FY NII guide of $8.6-8.8B bought +1.95%; July 2026 raise to $8.74-8.80B sold -2.29%. Guidance moves have not had a consistent sign on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The absence of a mid-quarter raise is itself a mild negative against a whisper above consensus: a search summary circulating that management 'now expects NII and fees at the upper end' could not be sourced to any 2026 document and the primary deck says unchanged. If the market expected a Q4 guide raise the whisper gap would be wider and the skew negative; both are small, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: FOMC statement 2026-09-16: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm (12-0 vote, 3.75-4.00%). Whisper and consensus: https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/FITB. The July guide itself is in the Q2 call transcript (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1914119-20260718, 2026-07-18).

findings.finding: The Comerica systems conversion of about 600,000 accounts and 293-300 branches over Labor Day weekend (completed 2026-09-08) produced public reports of customers unable to access accounts, crowded lobbies and long phone/online waits in Detroit on 2026-09-08/09, with the app and bill-pay unavailable for some; the quarter therefore carries roughly three weeks of post-conversion deposit and fee attrition risk that no public series measures, against management's July figures of 99.4% commercial-customer retention and consumer at 102% of the beginning-of-year level.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print on this name has carried a conversion quarter; the July print, where retention was reported as strong, fell 2.29% anyway.
findings.why_not_priced: Local-TV coverage of lobby queues is not in any analyst model; the company's 2026-09-15 deck says 'Conversion & Integration complete' and no sell-side note has flagged attrition. If it were priced, period-end deposit estimates would have been cut and they have not been (revenue consensus unchanged at $3.34B). It is a proxy for a number only the release will show.
findings.independence: WXYZ Detroit, same week: https://www.wxyz.com/news/fifth-third-banks-merger-with-comerica-frustrates-local-customers. Company completion release, 2026-09-08: https://www.dbusiness.com/daily-news/fifth-third-bancorp-completes-comerica-technology-and-brand-conversion/. Retention figures are from the Q2 call (shared document with finding 3).

findings.finding: The forward path is intact and visible: the 09-15 deck reiterates the $850M pre-tax run-rate expense synergy target for Q4 2026 as 'on track', Q3 adjusted expenses guided down 1-2% including ~$60M CDI amortisation, and the July call set buybacks at $50-100M in Q3 rising to a normalised $200-300M per quarter from Q4 with CET1 'effectively' at the 10-10.5% target (9.93% at Q2), so the release is likely to confirm Q4 capital return resuming at scale.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No repurchases in H1 2026 and the July print, which first announced the H2 resumption, fell 2.29%; this line has not been paid for yet.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside the guide and in every preview, so mostly priced; the residual is that a stock 15% off its high with a $61.71 average target (stockanalysis, 2026-10-08) gets a buyback restart confirmed into a drawdown. Sized near zero accordingly.
findings.independence: Buyback cadence and CET1 target from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1914119-20260718, 2026-07-18; shares a document with finding 3). Targets: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/fitb/forecast/.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is light rather than crowded: the stock is -15.25% from its 52-week high and -4.9% over 20 sessions in a sector-wide drawdown (PNC -12.6% since its last print as of 2026-10-06), short interest rose 12.6% in two weeks to 36.26M shares but is still only 4.0% of shares outstanding with 5.05 days to cover, the 25-delta skew is -0.35 (balanced) and put/call open interest is 0.42; a print that simply meets the guide lands on a lower base with no squeeze mechanism and no downside hedging premium to unwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: seven prints, median |move| 1.31%, max 2.29%; the option market's 5.79% implied is 4x the median realised, so the implied move is more likely to be overpriced than underpriced.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is the price, not a finding about the print; this is filed as positioning for the judges and sized small. If the drawdown had been FITB-specific the skew would be positive and the shorts larger; neither is the case.
findings.independence: Sealed baseline tape and options block (as of 2026-10-16T17:11Z). PNC drawdown: https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/pnc (data as of 2026-10-06).

outside_window.finding: Redemption at par of all $500M 1.707% fixed-to-floating senior notes due 2027 on 2026-11-01, announced by 8-K on 2026-09-24; routine liability management, no stated charge, retires a floating-rate funding line after the September hike.

searched_and_found_nothing: A mid-quarter guidance change: the 2026-09-14 8-K (Barclays deck) says Q3 expectations unchanged from July 17; the 'upper end' phrasing returned by one search summary could not be sourced to any 2026 document and was discarded.

Any FITB credit event in Q3 2026 (an 8-K, a named bankruptcy exposure, an NDFI or CRE charge-off): nothing since the Q3 2025 Tricolor charge; the only Sept-Oct 8-Ks are the Barclays deck, a registered-note exchange (2026-09-23, no financial impact) and the note redemption above.
Form 4 clusters: none filed between 2026-08-05 and 2026-10-16; the only insider filing is a Form 3 for a new EVP/CHRO (Megan Burkhart, event 2026-10-01).
Post-conversion deposit outflow data or October customer complaints: nothing beyond the 2026-09-08/09 Detroit TV reports; no Reddit or BBB thread with a date surfaced.
Analyst upgrades/downgrades in October 2026: none found; ratings 13 Strong Buy / 4 Buy / 5 Hold, average target $61.71 (stockanalysis, 2026-10-08).
Share-price reactions of PNC (10-15) and Truist (10-16) on their print days: not retrievable from any dated source; FITB's own 5-day run-up through the week is -0.64%.
The Q2 call Q&A tail (deposit betas, conversion cash build and its NIM effect): the transcript page's second half did not render.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly negative while the skew is balanced and the stock is already 15% off its high in a sector drawdown, so the evidence is partly in the price and sits against a damped reaction history (median 1.31% versus a 5.79% implied move), which is why p_up is 43 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (narrow proxy below the broader series): the PNC NII-guide shortfall is one peer, Truist landed in guide and JPM raised, so the read-through was cut from -0.6 to -0.4 and the mixed series is named in the finding.

Rule 5/7 (a drawdown is positioning, not a cause): the drawdown-into-print lean was trimmed from +0.4 to +0.3; short interest at 4.0% / 5 DTC was checked before the negatives and is not crowded, so no negative was shrunk for squeeze risk.
Rule 1 (reaction function over the fact): already in the draft via the sell-the-beat finding; p_up moved from 42 to 43 to reflect that the negatives are proxies, abs_move_pct left at 3.0.
Rule 6: bar sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing adjusted-EPS sources; the Nov 1 note redemption stays in outside_window. Nothing else changed.
